title: Louis versus Lewis, Chicago job help and a message to Louis
summary: Punch says they coined Satchmo, recalls Louis giving him jobs in Chicago before leaving for New York, and sends a get-well message.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Do you have a message for... Do you call him Lewis or Louis? What did...
I call him Sach. What did people say? Because some people say Lewis, some people say Louis.
Well, them, a lot of them don't like to say Sachmark. We started that down here, Sachmark.
And he liked that. He liked that word, Sach.
Well, he's always got some kind of mouth he's putting on somebody else.
So do you say Louis or Louis?

Louis told me at 46... 46 in South Park, we were here in Chicago. I was ridden so much sand. I'll tell you about that. I was ridden sand. So he told me, he said, look, I'm going to give you Chicago. I said, I'm going to New York. I said, okay. I thought he was kidding me. Yeah. Man, the next thing he did, Lewis was gone. That's when he gave me that job at the Vingdon. He gave me a lot of nice, good big jobs. I can't believe.
Mm-hmm. Oh, yeah, I can imagine.
Well, um... Do you have any message for him? Hmm?
Do you have a message for him?
Hope you'll recover. And be the same man he was always. That's pretty good. Yeah, that's a good one.
